steps.title: Load the specimen
steps.explanation: A one-second ramp raises the axial force to 0.6 N. Work splits into recoverable storage and viscous loss; both quantities come from the existing standard-linear-solid protocol.
steps.observe: Extension is about 1.68159 mm. Work 0.000531635 J equals storage 0.000434748 J plus loss 0.0000968864 J up to roundoff.

steps.title: Hold force and observe creep
steps.explanation: Keep force at 0.6 N during the hold. Extension keeps increasing, so the load continues doing work as the viscous branch evolves.
steps.observe: Extension grows to about 2.32895 mm while force remains 0.6 N. Storage plus accumulated loss still matches the displayed external work.

steps.title: Change what the fixture holds
steps.explanation: Replay from the same initial state and loading ramp, but hold extension after 1 s. With no further extension during the hold, no additional external work is done.
steps.observe: Extension stays 1.68159 mm; force relaxes to about 0.402942 N. Work remains 0.000531635 J while storage decreases and loss increases.

steps.title: Release and inspect finite recovery
steps.explanation: Return to the force-hold protocol and inspect its end after unloading from 3–4 s and recovery from 4–7 s. Zero applied force does not imply instantaneous recovery.
steps.observe: Force is zero, but residual extension is about 0.189097 mm and storage about 0.00000773842 J. Loss is 0.000511623 J; the finite run does not claim complete recovery.

audit.finding: Time scrubbing omitted applied force, phase and external work, and could not contrast creep with relaxation.
audit.change: Expose force versus extension holds and the complete work/storage/loss ledger at progressive protocol states.
audit.remaining: Passive small-strain axial SLS with prescribed cross-sections; no transverse contraction, activation, finite-strain tissue or irreversible plastic deformation.
